Blueprints · Architecture

Reference architecture

Nine layers make an agent-operated enterprise. The model is one layer. The harness, not the model, sets the autonomy ceiling.

Eight patterns

Architecture variations

  1. Assistant (L1). A person asks, a GPT-class model drafts, the person acts. Chat → Model gateway → Embeddings and retrieval (RAG) → Frontier large language models (GPT-class) → Decision trace → Accountable owner → Systems of record
  2. Single agent with tools (L2 to L3). One agent plans, calls governed tools and proposes; rules commit. Email → Context and memory → Finance agents → Frontier large language models (GPT-class) → Tool gateway → Policy and limits → Verification and approval → API gateway → Decision trace
  3. Supervisor and specialists (L3). A supervisor agent splits the goal; specialists work under cross-agent contracts. Web → Planner and supervisor agent → Cross-agent contracts → Supply chain agents → Finance agents → Verification and approval → Workflow engine → Approval inbox and decision cards → Decision trace store
  4. Event-driven IoT loop (L2 to L3). Sensor anomaly to work order, with a technician approving. IoT and edge sensors → IoT time series → Data quality gates → Edge and IoT analytics → Classical ML and forecasting → Event bus → Maintenance agents → Policy and limits → Approval inbox and decision cards → API gateway
  5. Voice front door (L3). Speech in, identity check, agent, speech out, and a warm handoff. Voice agents → Speech (speech-to-text, text-to-speech) → Identity and delegation → Service agents → Embeddings and retrieval (RAG) → Policy and limits → Speech (speech-to-text, text-to-speech) → Escalation
  6. Physical AI cell (L3 in envelope). A robot policy trained with reinforcement learning in a digital twin, deployed inside a safety envelope. Simulation and digital twins → Reinforcement learning (incl. human feedback, bandits) → Offline evals → Evaluation and kill switch → Physical AI (robot foundation models, vision-language-action policies) → Machine control interfaces → Robots and machines → Kill switch
  7. Optimizer and LLM (L3). A solver decides the plan; a GPT-class model explains it and handles exceptions. Event streams → Classical ML and forecasting → Optimization solvers → Frontier large language models (GPT-class) → Policy and limits → Approval inbox and decision cards → API gateway
  8. Graph-grounded agent (L2 to L3). A knowledge graph resolves entities and links before the agent acts. Email → Finance agents → Knowledge graphs and graph machine learning → Knowledge graph → Reasoning models → Policy and limits → Escalation → Decision trace

In words

The layers and their components

Channels and signals

  • Web. Forms and portals start requests. Use for: Structured requests with known fields. Not for: Free text that needs a conversation. PCS-01 PRV-04
  • Chat. People ask in natural language. Use for: Questions, status and simple changes. Not for: Decisions that need a signature. PRV-04 PCS-01 PCS-05
  • Email. Customers and suppliers send requests and documents. Use for: High-volume inbound requests. Not for: Instructions to the agent; email is data. PCS-01 PRV-01
  • Voice agents. Callers speak with an agent that listens and answers. Use for: Common requests with clear policy. Not for: Distressed callers or disputes; hand off fast. PRV-04 IAM-05 HO-03
  • Mobile. Field staff and customers use phone apps. Use for: Approvals on the move and field capture. Not for: Long reviews of complex evidence. HO-01 IAM-02
  • IoT and edge sensors. Sensors stream readings from assets and sites. Use for: Condition monitoring and early warning. Not for: Direct control of machines. OT-01 OT-02 OT-04
  • Robots and machines. Machines act in the physical world. Use for: Repetitive tasks in mapped spaces. Not for: Unmapped spaces shared with people. PHY-01 PHY-02 PHY-03

Human command

  • Charter. Leaders state intent, limits and the do-not-automate list. Use for: Before any agent goes live. Not for: As a one-time document; review it. TAL-05 HO-02
  • Approval inbox and decision cards. People decide on cards with evidence, rule and options. Use for: L2 steps and over-limit cases. Not for: Low-value, reversible items; let them run. HO-01 HO-05 SOD-01
  • Escalation. Hard cases reach the right person with full context. Use for: Low confidence, disputes and outages. Not for: As the default path for all work. HO-03 TAL-02
  • Kill switch. Owners stop an agent, a scope or the fleet. Use for: Always. Test it every quarter. Not for: Never skip the drill. RES-01 RES-04 PHY-03
  • Accountable owner. Each agent has one named person who answers for it. Use for: Every agent, every version. Not for: Shared or committee ownership. HO-02 IAM-02

Orchestration

  • Planner and supervisor agent. Splits a goal into tasks and assigns them. Use for: Multi-step goals across domains. Not for: Simple flows; a workflow engine is safer. RES-03 CST-01 TAL-03
  • Workflow engine. Runs fixed steps in a fixed order. Use for: Known processes with clear rules. Not for: Open-ended work. TAL-02 TRC-01
  • Event bus. Moves events between systems and agents in real time. Use for: Signals that need fast reaction. Not for: Batch data with no urgency. DQ-02 TRC-02
  • Cross-agent contracts. Define who decides, what evidence returns and what happens on failure. Use for: Any agent-to-agent handoff. Not for: Implicit handoffs by shared memory. TAL-03 HO-02
  • Queues. Hold work, set priority and absorb peaks. Use for: Volume spikes and retries. Not for: Hiding work that nobody owns. TAL-04 RES-03

Agents

  • Finance agents. Disputes, invoice exceptions, reconciliations, close. Use for: High-volume, rule-rich work. Not for: Payment release and bank changes. TAL-01 TAL-05 DQ-04
  • Supply chain agents. Planning, purchasing and supplier follow-up. Use for: Frequent, bounded decisions. Not for: Large commitments to third parties. TAL-01 CST-02
  • Service agents. Answer customers and change orders. Use for: Common requests with clear policy. Not for: Complaints that need empathy and judgment. HO-03 PCS-05
  • HR agents. Onboarding tasks, policy answers, scheduling. Use for: Admin work around people. Not for: Decisions about hiring, pay or dismissal. TAL-05 PRV-01 HO-01
  • Maintenance agents. Turn signals into work orders and plans. Use for: Condition-based maintenance. Not for: Direct machine control. OT-03 HO-01 DQ-03

Intelligence: model portfolio

  • Frontier large language models (GPT-class). Read, write and reason over language. Use for: Unstructured text, drafting, explanation. Not for: Arithmetic, postings and hard limits. PCS-01 PCS-02 MR-04
  • Small and open models. Cheaper, faster language models for narrow tasks. Use for: Classification, extraction, routing, edge. Not for: Broad open-ended reasoning. MR-01 TPS-01
  • Reasoning models. Plan and check multi-step problems. Use for: Planning, root cause, complex exceptions. Not for: Low-latency or low-cost paths. RES-03 CST-01 MR-04
  • Multimodal and vision. Read documents, images and video. Use for: Invoices, forms, inspections. Not for: Safety decisions without other checks. PCS-02 DQ-01
  • Speech (speech-to-text, text-to-speech). Turn voice into text and text into voice. Use for: Voice channels and hands-free work. Not for: Noisy settings without confirmation. PRV-04 PRV-02
  • Embeddings and retrieval (RAG). Find the right documents and ground answers in them. Use for: Policy answers and evidence packs. Not for: Facts that live in systems of record; query them. PCS-04 MR-04 DQ-02
  • Knowledge graphs and graph machine learning. Resolve entities and relationships. Use for: Suppliers, fraud rings, asset hierarchies. Not for: Simple lookups. DQ-03 MR-04
  • Classical ML and forecasting. Predict numbers, classes and time series. Use for: Demand, risk scores, anomalies. Not for: Language tasks. MR-01 MON-02
  • Optimization solvers. Find the best plan under constraints. Use for: Scheduling, routing, supply plans. Not for: Fuzzy goals that nobody can state. MR-01 TAL-01
  • Reinforcement learning (incl. human feedback, bandits). Learn actions from rewards over many trials. Use for: Sequential decisions with fast feedback. Not for: Live trials where errors are costly. MR-05 PHY-04 MON-03
  • Rules engines and RPA. Apply fixed logic and repeat screen tasks. Use for: Postings, limits, stable legacy screens. Not for: Judgment or changing screens. TAL-02 SOD-02
  • Simulation and digital twins. Model a plant, warehouse or network in software. Use for: Training and testing policies safely. Not for: As proof without field validation. MR-05
  • Edge and IoT analytics. Compact models score sensor streams next to the machine. Use for: Low-latency anomaly detection on equipment. Not for: Heavy models on small devices. OT-01 OT-04 MON-02
  • Physical AI (robot foundation models, vision-language-action policies). Perceive and act with robots. Use for: Picking, inspection, handling in mapped cells. Not for: Open spaces with people and no safety envelope. PHY-01 PHY-04 OT-03

Harness: control plane

  • Identity and delegation. One identity per agent, acting for an accountable person. Use for: Every agent call. Not for: Shared service accounts. IAM-01 IAM-02 IAM-05 OT-01
  • Registry and lifecycle. Only registered, active agent versions run. Use for: Every release. Not for: Shadow agents outside the registry. IAM-04 MR-03 HO-02 TRC-04
  • Policy and limits. Thresholds, segregation of duties and blackout windows, outside the model. Use for: Every action with value at risk. Not for: Limits in prompts. SOD-01 MR-06 TAL-01 TAL-05
  • Tool gateway. Scopes, rate limits, read and write separation. Use for: Every tool call. Not for: Direct database writes by agents. IAM-03 TAL-03 TAL-04 TAL-06
  • Model gateway. Routing, fallback, masking and quotas. Use for: Every model call. Not for: Direct calls to providers. PRV-02 PCS-03 PCS-05 RES-02
  • Context and memory. What may enter context and what memory may keep. Use for: Every prompt and memory write. Not for: Unfiltered documents in context. DQ-02 DQ-03 PRV-01 PCS-01
  • Verification and approval. Schema checks, a checker and approval cards. Use for: Before every commit. Not for: Self-checking by the same agent. SOD-03 DQ-01 PRV-04 MR-04
  • Operating envelope and cost. Deadlines, call budgets, retries and loop guards. Use for: Every run. Not for: Unlimited retries. RES-03 CST-01 CST-02
  • Decision trace. What was seen, decided and done. Use for: Every decision. Not for: Logs that miss the evidence. DQ-04 PRV-03 MON-04 TRC-01
  • Evaluation and kill switch. Test sets before release; stop an agent, a scope or the fleet. Use for: Every release and every quarter. Not for: Release without evals. SOD-02 MR-01 MR-02 MR-05

Tools and integration

  • API gateway. Exposes released interfaces of core systems. Use for: Every write to a system of record. Not for: Screen scraping where an interface exists. IAM-03 TAL-06
  • Tool contracts (MCP-style). Typed, scoped descriptions of what a tool does. Use for: Every tool an agent may call. Not for: Generic tools with broad scopes. TAL-03 IAM-03
  • RPA bots. Repeat screen steps on legacy systems. Use for: Stable screens with no interface. Not for: Changing screens or judgment. SOD-02 TAL-06
  • Machine control interfaces. Request setpoints and tasks behind safety controllers and interlocks. Use for: Plant and robot tasks. Not for: Bypassing the control system. OT-02 OT-03 PHY-01

Data and context

  • Systems of record. Ledgers, orders, assets, people. Use for: The source of truth for facts. Not for: As a scratchpad for agents. DQ-02 TAL-06
  • Data products. Curated, owned datasets with contracts. Use for: Planning, analytics and features. Not for: Ownerless copies. DQ-01 DQ-02
  • Vector store. Stores embeddings for retrieval. Use for: Policy and document search. Not for: Facts that change daily. PCS-04
  • Knowledge graph. Stores entities and relationships. Use for: Master data and fraud checks. Not for: Transaction data. DQ-03
  • Feature store. Serves consistent features to models. Use for: Classical ML in production. Not for: One-off analysis. MON-02 DQ-02
  • Event streams. Ordered streams of business events. Use for: Real-time agents. Not for: Data that needs heavy cleaning first. DQ-01
  • IoT time series. Sensor readings over time. Use for: Condition monitoring and twins. Not for: Without plausibility checks. OT-04
  • Data quality gates. Check freshness, completeness and validity. Use for: Before any agent reads. Not for: After the decision. DQ-01

Assurance

  • Offline evals. Test sets run before release. Use for: Every release and model change. Not for: Only once at launch. MR-01 TPS-03
  • Online evals. Score live outputs and samples. Use for: Every production step. Not for: Instead of offline evals. MON-01 HO-04
  • Red-teaming. Attack the system on purpose. Use for: Before release and after big changes. Not for: As a one-time event. PCS-01 PCS-03
  • Drift and quality monitoring. Detect shifts in data and outputs. Use for: All models in production. Not for: Without an owner to act. MON-02 MON-03
  • Decision trace store. Keeps traces append-only. Use for: Every decision. Not for: Editable logs. TRC-02 PRV-03
  • Audit. Independent review of controls and outcomes. Use for: Every promotion to L3 and above. Not for: Only after an incident. TRC-03 HO-04

Ceiling hints, levels and figures on this page are illustrative. Each company sets its own with internal audit.
